vonNeumann.plain: The Fock space $\mathcal{H}$ over $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ is separable and infinite dimensional. Coherent vectors $\varepsilon(b\hat g)$ built from real Schwartz tests $g$ through a fixed positive-time profile span it densely, and any family with the Gram table $\exp\langle u,v\rangle$ and dense span is carried onto it by exactly one unitary.

$U(t)$ multiplies the $n$-particle wavefunction by $e^{-it\sum_j\omega(k_j)}$: a group of unitaries with $U(0)=I$. The curve $t\mapsto U(t)\psi$ is differentiable at $0$ exactly when $\psi\in\operatorname{Dom}H$, with derivative $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H\psi$; $H$ is symmetric and nonnegative there.
Exactly one unitary carries the completed tensor product of two Fock spaces onto the Fock space over the direct sum, with $\varepsilon(u)\otimes\varepsilon(v)\mapsto\varepsilon(u\oplus v)$.
For every unit state $\psi$, exactly one weight on closed subspaces is nonnegative, normalized, countably additive and invariant under unitaries fixing $\psi$: the Born weight $\|P_K\psi\|^2$.

Every projection-valued measure $P$ on $\mathbb{R}$ gives a densely defined, exactly self-adjoint $A=\int a\,\mathrm{d}P(a)$ on $\operatorname{Dom}A=\{\psi:\int a^2\,\mathrm{d}\|P(a)\psi\|^2<\infty\}$, with expectation $\int a\,\mathrm{d}\|P(a)\psi\|^2$.

The pure update $P\psi/\|P\psi\|$ exists and is unique up to a phase. For every countable mixture $\rho$ the conditioned state is $P\rho P/\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)$, the operator certain of the event that keeps the subevent ratios is unique, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)$ is the same in every Hilbert basis.

wightman.plain: Second-quantized spacetime translations and all of $O(n+1)$ fix the vacuum and carry $\Phi(f)$ to the field of the moved test. Boosts along every direction form a one-parameter unitary group fixing the vacuum and intertwining the field.
For every finite set of momenta, $|\sum_i k_i|\le\sum_i\omega(k_i)$; every total energy is $0$ or at least $\hbar m$; the shift contracts the $n$-particle sector by $e^{-snm}$.
$H\Omega=0$, and for every $s>0$ the vectors fixed by the shift $e^{-sH/\hbar}$ are exactly the multiples of $\Omega$.

The finite-particle core is dense and contains $\Omega$; every matrix element $f\mapsto\langle\varphi,\Phi(f)\psi\rangle$ is continuous on spacetime Schwartz space; $\Phi(f)$ is symmetric for real $f$.
For real compactly supported tests whose supports satisfy $|t-t'|<|x-x'|$ point by point, $\Phi(f)\Phi(f')=\Phi(f')\Phi(f)$ on the core, in every dimension $D\ge 2$.
Polynomials in the fields of real Schwartz tests, applied to $\Omega$, span a dense subspace of the Fock space.

steps.plain: A law on $\mathbb{R}$ whose two independent copies are unchanged by every rotation is a centred Gaussian. No moment, density or continuity is assumed. The fair-sign pair fails: a $45^\circ$ rotation zeros its first coordinate half the time (fairSign_rot45_zeros_half).

On every finite graph with site mean square $S>0$ and edge ratio $\ell_{\min}0$ exactly when $r<\bar\ell$. It is centred with characteristic function $e^{-\xi^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}\xi/2}$ (gibbs_charFun) and reflection positive on every symmetric free box (freeBox_lattice_gibbs_reflection_pos).

As the lattice spacing goes to zero, the lattice covariance form tends to $\hbar\int\overline{\hat f}\,\hat g/(|p|^2+m^2)$ in every dimension, and with it every finite-list Gaussian characteristic value.

A positive nonconstant symbol whose opposite-pulse form is nonnegative is $a(x+m^2)$. For every degree $\ge 2$ an explicit smooth test supported in $s>0$ makes the reflected form strictly negative (smooth_normal_nogo_unconditional).

The plane reading $Q(h)$ and its time derivative $P(h)$ obey $[Q,P]=i\hbar$ and $\Delta Q\,\Delta P\ge\hbar/2$ on finite-particle states; and the one-particle evolution tends in $L^2$ to the free Schrödinger evolution $e^{-i\tau|k|^2/2m}$ (nonrelativistic_schrodinger_l2_limit).
A function bounded above on $[0,1]$ and additive there is linear. No continuity is assumed. This doubling-map argument is the one scalar step behind both the Gaussian law and the Born rule.

outside: A single countably additive measure on tempered distributions (Bochner–Minlos). The paper's law is the family of finite-list laws, which is what the file works with.
The position-space bridge from finite free boxes to $(-\Delta+m^2)^{-1}$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^D)$. The momentum-space limit is proved.

Reflection positivity in the continuum for general nonlinear preparations, and positivity and nonconstancy of the symbol, which enter §2.4 as hypotheses. Finite-box reflection positivity and the continuum kernel factorization are proved.

The identification of the Fock space with $L^2$ of a measure on the plane, and the multiplication law of the full Poincaré group. Translations, rotations and boosts are each proved to fix $\Omega$ and intertwine the field.
The converse spectral theorem, that every self-adjoint operator comes from a projection-valued measure. The direction the paper uses is proved.
